New children streaming to a parent with storage mode `dbengine` will now have their metrics stored in the parent's database. 
Old children that already have a database created in the parent will continue to use that one to store metrics.

issue_context.title: Assign new children to localhost multidb
issue_context.body:
#### Summary
By activating the localhost multidb functionality children that connect to the parent to begin streaming and are configured to use dbengine will fall into two categories by checking the existence of datafiles (under the `machine_guid/dbengine` folder)

- Currently in memory - already stored in the localhost multi db.
- Datafiles already exist
  - The child will connect in legacy mode
     - Data collection and metadata log files will continue to be under `machine_guid/dbengine/`
     - Datafile maximum size for the child will be `dbengine disk space`
  - Data is only accessible when the child connects
    - dbegine initialization and metadata log replay will be done on connect (as it is done now)

- Datafiles do not exist
  - The child will use the localhost multidb
     - data collection and metadata log files will be under the main `dbengine/` folder
     - The maximum datafile size for the localhost multidb will be defined by a new configuration parameter `dbengine multihost disk space`. See #9452 
  - Metadata log replay is done when the parent starts
    - Children (HOSTs) will be in archived mode until streaming is established
    - Charts will be created in archived mode (until collection for that chart starts)


##### Queries
Verify that queries work as then dbengine context is shared between localhost and children

review_comments: What's the difference with `while(localhost) rrdhost_free(localhost);`? It looks the same to me.

> What's the difference with `while(localhost) rrdhost_free(localhost);`? It looks the same to me.

I want child-hosts to be released before the localhost. This ensures that a child on multihost will flush out any metrics. If the parent shutdowns first it will kill the dbengine. 

This will also help with the checks that were added to 

```
rrdeng_store_metric_flush_current_page
```

It's about the dashboard not showing all archived hosts in the top left corner, because they are empty.

It's unreachable, not archived. This is the same even today, you can actually lookup the data. If you restart the agent it will be archived.

the list seems to me before this PR as "Any child node that ever connected to agent" but it gets lost after an agent restarts.

Wouldn't it be better after this PR "Any child node that ever connected to agent" but now we actually keep history between restarts?

Anyway, I will not block PR on this comment so I mark it resolved.
